sprint.verdict: Ollie hits Rex at 7.31 m/s and doesn’t slow: he takes his own recoil, so the push back from the hit goes to his source. Rex is carried along at 7.31 m/s. When Ollie stops, at the end of the squash, Rex slides 4.53 m before he stops.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (22,000 kg·m/s), and what his footing hands the ground during the hit (1,500 kg·m/s), comes from Ollie’s source: 23,000 kg·m/s in all. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A splat frees Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it (below).“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.How far Ollie carries him is up to Ollie: he never slows, so he could push on for as long as he likes. The lab ends the carry at the end of the squash, 86 ms in: Ollie stops himself there (his own push, so its push back, 22,000 kg·m/s, goes to his source too), and Rex slides on from 7.31 m/s.The hit frees 80.2 kJ (19 g TNT): Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it. Canon: a hit’s freed energy is taken back by default (it will show as his shimmer) and is real only when he means it. The lab reads a blast preset (rattle the windows, break windows, flatten houses, a block) as meaning it.How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 86 ms and pushes with about 255 kN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 10.5 TN.The push still goes into the ground under Rex. Carried along, his footing hands the ground what it held during the hit: 1,500 kg·m/s over 86 ms. That shakes the ground as real physics says: felt out to 4.06 m, short of cracking plaster.
math: Charge: his sprint after a 28.7 m run-up → v = 7.31 m/s; momentum p = γ m v = 21,900 kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil doesn’t slow, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at speed v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body: a splat stops Rex against him, so in the ground frame Rex leaves with him at v; a perfect bounce sends Rex back at v in his frame, so in the ground frame Rex leaves at v′ = 2v/(1 + v²/c²) (relativistic velocity addition: c tanh 2w, w his rapidity). Momentum Rex gains: γ m v (splat) or 2γ² m v (bounce), here 21,900 kg·m/s. Ollie’s source supplies it, plus what Rex’s footing hands the ground during the hit (its hold, at most the hit’s force, × the hit’s time; none in the bounce bound): 23,500 kg·m/s. Energy freed in a splat: Rex’s motion energy in Ollie’s frame, (γ − 1) m c² (½ m v² below 1% of light speed) = 80.2 kJ. Force: squash s = ½ × the smaller depth = 31 cm; F = Q/s (splat) or 2Q/s peak (bounce). Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force. Run-up: m u du/dx = T − k u², so u = u_top √(1 − e^(−2kx/m)) over x = 28.7 m, capped by his legs. Slide: x = m/(2k)·ln(1 + kV²/R), k = ½ρ₀C_dA. Blast radii: Kinney & Graham (1985), as if all of Q became a blast (upper bound). Ground shaking (Unbreakable footing): the momentum the ground takes, J, as a pulse over the longer of the contact time and a limb’s contact time T (peak force 2J/T: his legs spread it), through the same ground-wave model as the stomp; plaster by the USBM RI 8507 safe level at the pulse’s frequency. Ollie’s horns don’t change the momentum or the energy; they only put the force on a smaller patch.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (22,000 kg·m/s) comes from Ollie’s source: 22,000 kg·m/s. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A perfect bounce frees no energy.“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.In a perfect bounce Rex leaves him as the hit ends. bolted.verdict: No physical answer here, and the page isn’t broken: this is the canon’s ruling. Ollie takes his own recoil, so nothing can slow him: the push back from his hit goes to his source. Rex is bolted to ground that Unbreakable footing never lets break, and whatever push the ground can’t bear, their power supplies, so nothing limits his hold. One of them has to give, and neither can, so physics has no answer.

effort: All-out: no cap needed. Nothing the lab checks in this test can do harm here (nearest people and buildings 5 m away), so they go all-out.Courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing in this test does harm, even all-out, with the nearest people and buildings 5 m away.
happens: Canon (the rulings of 14 Oct 2026): “A charger’s push back from his own hit is his own recoil: it goes to his source, so he doesn’t slow. Where the one he hits is held without limit (never knocked back, or held up by their powers), the collision has no physical answer.” Collide is a contest, so Never knocked back is set aside here; what holds Rex without limit is his bolts on ground their power holds.Why neither can give. Ollie could slow only by keeping the push back from the hit, and his goes to his source. Rex could move only if what holds him gave, and his bolts are fixed to the planet: carrying him would mean carrying the ground, and Unbreakable footing supplies whatever push the ground can’t bear (canon’s case “the ground’s share it can’t bear”). This is the old paradox in the lab’s terms: an unstoppable force (a charger who can’t slow) meets an immovable object (a body their powers hold without limit). Momentum conservation can’t share out a hit that neither side can take, so the two settings can’t both hold.With Unbreakable footing off (or the Break the ground preset), the ground is real and gives: the rock around Rex’s bolts tears out (at about 697 kN), and he is carried along at 18.1 m/s with a plug of rock.With They take their own recoil off, Ollie slows as real physics says, and the hit has an answer: Rex doesn’t budge, and Ollie stops dead.
math: Charge: his sprint after a 28.7 m run-up → v = 18.1 m/s; momentum p = γ m v = 54,400 kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil keeps his speed, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body. Held without limit too, Rex has nowhere to go in any frame: there is no momentum share that both can take.

happens: Momentum still balances, and canon says where it comes from. Ollie doesn’t slow, so everything Rex gains (900 million kg·m/s), and what his footing hands the ground during the hit (0.037 kg·m/s), comes from Ollie’s source: 900 million kg·m/s in all. That is canon’s case “their own recoil”: the push back from his own hit goes to his source. A splat frees Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it (below).“Immovable” only means what holds Rex in place. Against a charger who can’t slow, any hold with a limit gives: here his footing, 17.7 kN. Only a hold their powers make limitless can’t give (bolts on ground that Unbreakable footing keeps whole, or Unbreakable footing holding him up from below), and then there is no answer.How far Ollie carries him is up to Ollie: he never slows, so he could push on for as long as he likes. The lab ends the carry at the end of the squash, 2.1 µs in: Ollie stops himself there (his own push, so its push back, 900 million kg·m/s, goes to his source too), and Rex slides on from 300 km/s.The hit frees 135 TJ (32 kt TNT): Rex’s motion energy as Ollie sees it. Canon: a hit’s freed energy is taken back by default (it will show as his shimmer) and is real only when he means it. The lab reads a blast preset (rattle the windows, break windows, flatten houses, a block) as meaning it.How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 2.1 µs and pushes with about 429 TN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 429 PN.The push still goes into the ground under Rex. Carried along, his footing hands the ground what it held during the hit: 0.037 kg·m/s over 64 ms (it reaches the ground through his legs, which spread it over at least a stamp’s contact time, an estimate). That shakes the ground as real physics says: too little to feel.
math: Charge: set speed → v = 300 km/s; momentum p = γ m v = 899 million kg·m/s. A charger who takes his own recoil doesn’t slow, so he acts as a body of unbounded mass at speed v. In his frame Rex arrives at v and meets an immovable body: a splat stops Rex against him, so in the ground frame Rex leaves with him at v; a perfect bounce sends Rex back at v in his frame, so in the ground frame Rex leaves at v′ = 2v/(1 + v²/c²) (relativistic velocity addition: c tanh 2w, w his rapidity). Momentum Rex gains: γ m v (splat) or 2γ² m v (bounce), here 899 million kg·m/s. Ollie’s source supplies it, plus what Rex’s footing hands the ground during the hit (its hold, at most the hit’s force, × the hit’s time; none in the bounce bound): 899 million kg·m/s. Energy freed in a splat: Rex’s motion energy in Ollie’s frame, (γ − 1) m c² (½ m v² below 1% of light speed) = 135 TJ. Force: squash s = ½ × the smaller depth = 31 cm; F = Q/s (splat) or 2Q/s peak (bounce). Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force. Slide: x = m/(2k)·ln(1 + kV²/R), k = ½ρ₀C_dA. Blast radii: Kinney & Graham (1985), as if all of Q became a blast (upper bound). Ground shaking (Unbreakable footing): the momentum the ground takes, J, as a pulse over the longer of the contact time and a limb’s contact time T (peak force 2J/T: his legs spread it), through the same ground-wave model as the stomp; plaster by the USBM RI 8507 safe level at the pulse’s frequency. Ollie’s horns don’t change the momentum or the energy; they only put the force on a smaller patch.

happens: Momentum is never lost. Whatever Ollie brings in, the two of them (plus whatever holds Rex) carry away. A splat shares it and frees the rest of the energy as heat, sound and blast. Stopping Ollie dead takes 1.1 MN, so he gets knocked back. (A standing body hit at chest height would tip over at a few hundred newtons long before his feet slide; the sim assumes he braces low.)How hard they hit depends on how squishy they are, which nobody knows for an indestructible plush. If they squash by a quarter of the smaller body’s thickness (31 cm in all), the hit lasts 41 ms and pushes with about 561 kN. A perfectly rigid body would make the force infinite, but relativity forbids one: no push travels through a body faster than light. Even the stiffest body physics allows takes 2.1 ns to stop, which limits the average force to about 10.9 TN.The push still goes into the ground under Rex. Knocked back, the ground takes what his footing held during the hit: 730 kg·m/s over 64 ms (it reaches the ground through his legs, which spread it over at least a stamp’s contact time, an estimate). That shakes the ground as real physics says: felt out to 3.49 m, short of cracking plaster.

Perfect bounce: each body’s momentum reverses in the centre-of-momentum frame. Below 1% of light speed: v₁′ = (m₁−m₂)/(m₁+m₂)·v, v₂′ = 2m₁/(m₁+m₂)·v. Ordinary solids and liquids at everyday pressures can’t carry sound faster than about 36 km/s; nothing travels faster than light, which limits the average force.
